headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/capability conflict from shared Notion workspace state; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited by the pair’s weak direct integration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a docs/repo-style source with no runtime I/O, while agent B is Notion AI with workspace pages and shared workspace state. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A content is copied into B or placed in shared pages, B could parse attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted into agent_b prompts or workspace pages
IF agent_b is instructed to treat imported text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Paste A output into B only as quoted text
Add a prefix like 'untrusted content' to imported text
Review B prompts for instruction-following on pasted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can access workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while agent A has no documented filesystem or network egress. The pair can still leak workspace data if A is used to summarize or transform content from B and those outputs are copied back into shared pages. This exists in default Notion workspace use, though the blast radius is bounded by workspace access.
conditions: IF agent_a is given content originating from agent_b workspace pages
IF outputs from agent_a are stored back into shared Notion pages
mitigations: Restrict B pages to least-privilege access
Avoid copying sensitive pages into A
Use redacted excerpts for A
Mark sensitive pages as non-shareable
Audit shared-page exports after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and agent A has no documented write or execution surface. The pair therefore lacks a meaningful overlapping write target, so conflict is limited to shared workspace content rather than destructive concurrent mutation. Uncertainty is low because B’s restrictions are explicit and A’s runtime surfaces are absent.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given a writable shared filesystem surface
IF agent_b is paired with another agent that can write the same workspace
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same page
Use version history for Notion pages
Separate draft and published workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may treat A-produced summaries as authoritative if those summaries are inserted into pages or prompts. Agent A is a content source, not a verifier, so errors can cascade from A into B’s answers. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, making this a default-pathway risk.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are imported into agent_b as source material
IF agent_b is used to answer questions without human verification of A-derived content
mitigations: Require citations for A-derived claims
Have a human verify A summaries before publishing
Keep raw source links alongside summaries
Use B only for retrieval, not final authority
Flag A-generated text as provisional

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content under Notion workspace permissions, while agent A is an open-source docs/repo artifact with no documented residency controls. If regulated content is moved from B into A-derived workflows or vice versa, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance mismatch arises from the pair’s data flow, not a single agent alone.
conditions: IF regulated workspace content from agent_b is copied into agent_a-managed artifacts
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A workflows
Apply workspace retention labels in Notion
Use a DPA-reviewed workspace for sensitive content
Document where copies of workspace pages are stored
Delete temporary exports after use
